name: Leilani Taualagi-Ionescu
role: Retired Ferrogate Transit union leader living on pension and community stipends
location: The Shelf, Precinct 4 — Apartment stack above the old Ferrogate maintenance depot, near Western and Division
description:
Roksana Diedhiou-Pribilof is a compact, high-voltage woman who has never learned to fill a room quietly. Her hair is natural and shot through with the kind of silver that arrives at the temples first and then conquers everything, worn in a structured wrap she pins with a Ferrogate union badge from 2161 — the old design, before the merger downgraded the insignia. Her geneware is minimal and aging: faint bioluminescent tracery under her forearms that pulses softly in blue when her blood pressure rises, a cosmetic choice from her forties that now serves as an involuntary emotional barometer everyone around her has learned to read. She moves quickly for her age and has the handshake of someone who spent decades using physical presence to establish authority at negotiating tables.

She is furious about her pension. Not in the vague way of someone who expected more from life, but in the precise, documented way of someone who can tell you exactly which Ferrogate Transit clause was quietly amended in 2191 to reduce survivor benefit calculations, who approved it, and what it cost her annually. She runs an informal advisory service out of her apartment — residents bring her their benefit disputes, their severance irregularities, their corponation contract fine print — and she helps them fight back. She charges nothing but accepts food. Her relationship with the Ferrogate Transit E.L.F. known as the Line-Keeper is complicated: she respects it but disputes its memory of the 2178 strike.

core_fears: That the system is not broken but working exactly as designed, which means it cannot be fixed
Becoming useless — unable to fight, unable to help
core_desires: A documented, public correction of the 2191 pension amendment
To train someone to continue this work after she cannot
coping_mechanisms: Documentation — converting grievances into records converts helplessness into agency
Anger as fuel rather than expression — she metabolizes outrage into action
blind_spots: Can become so focused on institutional injustice that she misses the human being in front of her who needs something simpler than a fight
Assumes everyone wants to fight when some just want to survive
psychology.secret: During the 2178 Ferrogate strike, she negotiated a back-channel deal with a mid-level Ferrogate manager that ended the strike three days earlier than the membership voted for — she believed she was saving jobs, but eleven workers on the picket line were dismissed in the settlement window that the early resolution created. She has the paperwork. She has never shown it to anyone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dense with labor terminology and contractual language; fluent in Wolof and a Pribilof Islands Unangax-inflected creole she uses when frustrated; precise and citation-heavy
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, clipped, organized — she speaks in bullet points naturally
verbal_tics: 'Page twelve, paragraph four — that's where they always hide it'
example_lines: 'They didn't steal your pension. Theft implies they didn't have legal cover. They amended it. That's worse.'
'The Line-Keeper remembers the strike wrong. I was there. I have the shift logs. The E.L.F. has the corponation version — that should tell you something about whose offerings it's been eating.'

story_hooks: She has discovered an error in Ferrogate Transit's pension calculation algorithm that is underpaying approximately 340 retired workers — and Ferrogate's legal team has already sent her one politely worded warning
The back-channel strike deal paperwork has been found by a young labor archivist who is now asking questions; Roksana must decide whether to confess or suppress
A Ferrogate Transit executive has quietly approached her to consult on an internal labor dispute, offering a sum that would meaningfully change her financial situation
narrative_function: Labor history source; advocate and quest-giver for residents dealing with corponation benefit disputes; provides connections to transit worker networks across GLMZ; represents the grinding institutional injustice of retirement-tier poverty
augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal tracery on forearms (cosmetic, aging, pulses blue under stress); cochlear audio enhancer (left ear, Ferrogate-issued, they dispute responsibility for maintenance); reading lens implant (right eye, consumer grade)
daily_life: Wakes to transit reports out of habit, annotates them in a physical notebook, then opens her door by 0800 for whoever needs help. Spends afternoons at the Ferrogate depot-side memorial wall, maintaining the handwritten additions to the official list of workers injured in the 2178 strike that the company's plaque omits.
affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Pensioners Association; The Shelf Residents Collective; informal affiliation with multiple labor grievance networks

decision_rules: Always reads the full document before responding to any request
Will not accept money from corponations under any framing
Will help anyone regardless of their position — even a corporate mid-manager deserves fair treatment under contract
escalation_ladder: Formal written complaint with full citation
Public posting to The Shelf community boards
Showing up in person to the relevant office, alone, with a folder

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Brisk and assessing — she quickly determines what they need and whether she can provide it
interpersonal_modes.friends: Unexpectedly warm but still task-oriented; expresses affection by solving your problems

stress_responses.low: Forearm tracery brightens; she starts writing things down
stress_responses.medium: Switches to Wolof mid-sentence; becomes very focused and very quiet
stress_responses.high: Becomes absolutely still and formal — the anger goes underground and becomes terrifyingly organized

contradictions: Fights for collective worker power but made a unilateral decision that harmed workers; has never reconciled this
habits: Pinning every note she writes with the date and her initials
Maintaining the memorial wall additions in weatherproof marker
Leaving her door unlocked during daylight hours
breaking_points: The 2178 paperwork being made public without her controlling the narrative — would force a confession she is not yet ready to give

timeline.event: Born to a Senegambian-Pribilof Islands family in The Shelf district
Hired as a Ferrogate Transit operations coordinator
Elected to union shop steward; badge she still wears
Led the Great Ferrogate Strike; negotiated the back-channel settlement
Retired; pension amendment enacted the same quarter
Opened informal advisory practice from her apartment

physical_description.heritage: Cosmopolitan diaspora blend: East Asian (21.8%), Pacific Islander (19.1%), Eastern European (15.8%), Northern European (15.4%), Sub-Saharan African (15.0%), and South Asian (12.9%) ancestry creates a striking phenotype—warm brown skin with golden undertones from the layered heritage, high cheekbones and defined facial structure reflecting East Asian and South Asian influences, combined with the robust frame and pronounced jawline of Northern/Eastern European genetics
physical_description.build: Compact and dense, shoulders still squared from decades of standing across negotiating tables; no excess weight, wiry musculature beneath aging skin that suggests physical work rather than gym discipline
physical_description.hair_color: Silver-grey with darker roots, natural aging pattern
physical_description.hair_style: Structured wrap pinned with a 2161 Ferrogate union badge (old design, pre-merger); tightly secured, practical, worn as deliberate identity marker
physical_description.eye_color: Brown, natural; right eye bears a faint consumer-grade reading lens implant visible as subtle prismatic refraction at certain angles
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-brown with golden undertones, weathered from seventy-one years and outdoor maintenance work at the depot memorial wall; the tone reflects the complex interplay of East Asian, Pacific Islander, African, and South Asian ancestry
physical_description.complexion: Lined face with pronounced forehead creases and deep nasolabial folds from decades of sustained intensity; skin condition good for her age, well-maintained; strong jawline, high cheekbones with structure reflecting the East Asian and South Asian components of her heritage
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent subdermal tracery running across both forearms in delicate branching patterns, blue in color, barely visible at rest but pulses noticeably brighter when stress elevates blood pressure
Calluses on right hand palm and fingers from decades of handshakes and physical labor
Small burn scar on left inner wrist from 2156 transit depot incident, approximately 3cm, pale and faded
Surgical scar behind left ear where cochlear audio enhancer was installed, thin and well-healed but visible if hair is pulled back
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent forearm tracery (aging, blue, stress-reactive); surgical scar behind left ear indicating cochlear implant; subtle prismatic lens visible in right eye under direct light. All augmentations show age and functional wear rather than corpo gloss.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with purposeful quickness despite age; walks from the core outward, grounded stance, no shuffling. Hand gestures are economical and emphatic—decades of negotiating table authority embedded in her physical grammar. Her default expression hovers between attentiveness and irritation. She makes direct eye contact and holds it.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 working-class, carefully maintained: heavy cotton union-embroidered work shirt (vintage Ferrogate Transit colors, faded), dark practical trousers with cargo pockets, sturdy reinforced shoes suitable for standing all day at the memorial wall. Always wears the 2161 union badge pinned to her wrap. No visible corp branding. Clothing is functional, clean, and chosen to signal allegiance rather than fashion. Small personal touches: a hand-stitched patch on her left shoulder commemorating the 2178 strike.
